summary: Instagram is doing nearly all the work: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 50 views. The best videos show a simple robot or sensor with a surprising 'it can't see/hear/think, yet it works' idea, and those earn the most likes, saves and shares. Everyday-object explainers (taps, doors, smoke alarms, touchscreens, smartwatches) and the one English video get little attention, and the newest posts are too fresh to judge fully.
winningPattern: Hindi, Instagram-first. Subject is a hands-on robot or Arduino-style sensor project (gyro robot, clap switch, PIR, IR obstacle robot, line follower, mic). Hook is a short 'myth-breaking' line: the device lacks an ability (no brain, can't see, only hears noise) yet works. Titles are short Hinglish statements with one emoji and #shorts, with a surprising claim rather than a plain 'how does X work' question.
doMore: Make robot and Arduino module videos that show the build or behaviour, such as balancing, obstacle avoidance and line following
Open every video with a 'X can't do Y, yet it works' hook in the first line
Post Instagram-first and reuse the same video on YouTube with a stronger, searchable title
Lean on save-worthy content like clap switch or gyro explainers with a simple circuit shown on screen
Keep posting a steady 1-2 videos per day in the strong topics and check results after 48 hours
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' questions about public objects like mall doors, washroom taps and lifts
Posting near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector videos, two IR sensor videos, two tap videos) in the same week
Switching to English narration without a test plan, since it got no Instagram reach
